deep.reconstruction:
The page has no text, only a coloured drawing. It belongs to the 1983-84 study of 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', meaning arrangements of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane. The model used is the closed disk with antipodal boundary points identified.

What the drawing shows:
- **The disk and its marked points.** A yellow-green circle bounds the disk. Two black points sit on the boundary, at left (about 9 o'clock) and right (about 3 o'clock). They are nearly antipodal, so they most likely represent one and the same point at infinity of the projective plane.
- **The pseudo-lines.** Orange and brown curves run boundary to boundary; these are the pseudo-lines of the arrangement.
- **The grey hatching.** Fine, roughly horizontal, parallel grey pencil lines fill the disk. They run in the direction of the two black points, so they plausibly depict a pencil of 'parallel' pseudo-lines through that point at infinity. Such a pencil gives a sweep direction or a coordinate fibration of the disk.
- **The shaded band.** A yellow/orange band crosses the disk from top to bottom. A green dashed curve runs down its middle; this is a distinguished pseudo-line.
- **The band's structure.** Thick dark-brown polygonal contours bound the band. Short dark-blue segments cut across it, dividing it into a chain of cells.

Most natural reading: the band is the zone of the dashed pseudo-line, i.e. the union of the 2-cells of the arrangement that this pseudo-line crosses. The blue transverse segments are pieces of the other pseudo-lines that it crosses. The brown polygonal boundary is the outer boundary of the cells in the zone, drawn combinatorially rather than along the actual curves.

Purpose, judged from the neighbouring pages:
- **Previous page.** It counts crossings on a line through two points that are centres of pencils: 2n − [(ν−1)+(ν′−1)] = n − (ν′−1). This is bookkeeping of how many pseudo-lines a given line meets outside the two pencil centres.
- **Next page.** It studies the space 𝒳 of non-super-singular relative positions and the monodromy π₁(𝒳, D) → Aut Pol(D) ≅ 𝔻_{2n}, acting on circumscribed polygons. It also uses 'demi-tour' loops around an edge or a vertex.
- **Role of this figure.** It is a visual aid for these arguments: how a distinguished pseudo-line and its zone of cells sit relative to the rest of the arrangement and to a pencil through a point at infinity. Plausibly it prepares the deformation or 'franchissement' moves in which one pseudo-line is pushed across a vertex.

No statement, computation or new definition is recorded on this page.
errors: No mathematical assertions on the page, so nothing to check. The drawing is schematic: the brown band boundary does not follow the orange pseudo-lines exactly, so it should be read combinatorially, not as an exact cell decomposition.

ideas.what: Disk model of RP^2 with antipodal boundary points marking a single point at infinity, carrying an arrangement of pseudo-lines

ideas.where_published: Not in his published works; the pseudo-line material exists only in the Montpellier archive notes (cote 154).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely illustrative coloured figure with no text. It depicts standard objects: a pseudo-line arrangement, the zone of a pseudo-line, and a pencil through a point at infinity. Its only interest is as context for the monodromy and dihedral-group argument on the next page.
transcription_corrections: The transcription's description is accurate. Two additions: the two black boundary points are nearly antipodal (left at about 9 o'clock, right slightly lower at about 3 o'clock), consistent with the projective identification. The dark-blue transverse segments inside the band separate it into a chain of cells, consistent with a zone.
Faint mirror-image dot-matrix printing at the bottom is show-through from the back of the computer paper and is not part of the notes.
Page number '84' at the bottom left is in pencil.
